source: MITRE CWE 5.0 (2026-10-28), Research Concepts view (CWE-1000) ChildOf/ParentOf relations, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/<n>.html. Each key accepts itself, its direct children, and only the direct parent or sibling classes static tools commonly emit for it. Matching is one-way: a key accepts the listed report CWEs; nothing is implied in reverse.

CWE-22.rationale: Children CWE-23 (relative) and CWE-36 (absolute) path traversal. Parent CWE-706 is too broad.

CWE-78.rationale: Parent CWE-77 command injection, which tools report for OS command construction.

CWE-89.rationale: Child CWE-564 (Hibernate SQL injection). Parent CWE-943 is too broad.

CWE-121.rationale: Parents CWE-787 and CWE-788; sibling CWE-120 (child of 787); grandparent CWE-119 and its buffer-length children CWE-805/806, which C/C++ analyzers report for stack buffer overflows.

CWE-125.rationale: Children CWE-126 (over-read) and CWE-127 (under-read); parent CWE-119; sibling CWE-788 (after end of buffer), reported by cppcheck for out-of-bounds indexing.

CWE-134.rationale: No children; parent CWE-668 is too broad. Tools report CWE-134 itself.

CWE-190.rationale: Child CWE-680 (integer overflow to buffer overflow chain). Parent CWE-682 is too broad.

CWE-253.rationale: Parent CWE-754 and sibling CWE-252 (unchecked return value, also a child of 754), which tools report for mishandled return values.

CWE-327.rationale: Children CWE-328 (weak hash), CWE-780 (RSA without OAEP), CWE-1240. Parent CWE-693 is too broad.

CWE-362.rationale: Direct children (signal handler race, race within a thread, TOCTOU, context switching race, alternate channel race, permission race, write-once race, hardware logic race). Parent CWE-662 is too broad.

CWE-369.rationale: No children; parent CWE-682 is too broad.

CWE-401.rationale: Parent CWE-772 (missing release of resource), reported by leak checkers.

CWE-415.rationale: Parents CWE-1341 (multiple releases of same resource) and CWE-825 (expired pointer dereference). Parent CWE-666 is too broad.

CWE-416.rationale: Parent CWE-825 (expired pointer dereference). Peer CWE-415 is a distinct weakness.

CWE-476.rationale: CWE-690 is the chain unchecked return value to NULL pointer dereference ending in CWE-476. Parents CWE-710 and CWE-754 are too broad.

CWE-522.rationale: Direct children (plaintext storage, recoverable format, password in configuration file, weak encoding, unprotected transport, missing field masking). Parents CWE-1390 and CWE-668 are too broad.

CWE-617.rationale: No children; parent CWE-705 is too broad.

CWE-628.rationale: Direct children (wrong argument order, number, type, value, variable). Parent CWE-573 is too broad.

CWE-674.rationale: Child CWE-776 (recursive entity references). Parent CWE-834 is too broad for recursion.

CWE-761.rationale: Parent CWE-763 (release of invalid pointer), reported by allocator checkers for offset frees.

CWE-770.rationale: Children CWE-774 (file descriptors), CWE-789 (memory allocation with excessive size), CWE-1325; parent CWE-400 (uncontrolled resource consumption), commonly reported for unbounded allocation. Parent CWE-665 is unrelated in practice.

CWE-787.rationale: Direct children (classic, stack, heap overflow, write-what-where, underwrite, path manipulation without size); parent CWE-119; siblings CWE-788 and CWE-805, which cppcheck and CodeQL report for out-of-bounds writes.

CWE-798.rationale: Children CWE-259 (hard-coded password) and CWE-321 (hard-coded cryptographic key).

CWE-822.rationale: No children; parent CWE-119 would accept unrelated memory errors.

CWE-835.rationale: Parent CWE-834 (excessive iteration), reported for unbounded loops.

CWE-843.rationale: Parent CWE-704 (incorrect type conversion or cast), reported for type confusion.
